findings.claim: `raceAbortSignals` is dropped from the imports; if any remaining code in this file still references it the module will fail to compile, and if the call site was removed as part of this change it silently drops per-request abort-signal racing.
findings.rationale: The hunk only shows the import list, so I cannot see the body of httpBatchLink.ts. In the current tRPC batch link, `raceAbortSignals` is normally used to combine the batch's aggregate signal (`allAbortSignals`) with a per-request/abort-on-unmount signal so the in-flight fetch is cancelled when either fires. Removing the import means either (a) a dangling reference remains -> TS2304 build break, or (b) the racing behaviour was deleted, which changes cancellation semantics: the HTTP request would now only abort when *all* batched callers abort (allAbortSignals), never when an individual one does. Both outcomes are worth verifying. Medium confidence, since the rest of the file isn't visible in this hunk.
